item.title: Two German courts now hold Google liable for what its AI overviews say
item.description:
【the-decoder.com】Google tried to overturn a landmark Munich ruling on AI search liability by appealing, then quietly settled. The strategy isn't working. The Aachen Regional Court just applied the exact same reasoning in a new case where Google's AI falsely attributed criminal offenses to a doctor that actually involved someone else. A consistent legal view is forming across German courts, and it treats Google's AI answers as the company's own content. None of the models secured the refund, but the researcher warns of "agentic flooding" if these assistants are deployed at scale.
